extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying stochastic processes / Brownian motion
extracted.subtask_description: Rigorous conditions, theorems, and proof techniques for one- and multi-dimensional Brownian motion (stopping times, strong Markov property, martingales, Itô formula) and their applications (hitting times, embeddings, Donsker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feller property (markov process theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Markov process theory (ii) is called the Feller property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as the standard name for a continuity property of the semigroup in Markov process theory (appears as an item in a list of properties earlier in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Markov property (formula for shifted functionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stopping time S and suitable process Y, Ex( Y_S ◦ θ_S ; A ∩ {S < ∞} ) = Ex( E_{B(S)} Y_S ; A ∩ {S < ∞} ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by breaking event by values of S, applying the Markov property at deterministic times then summing; to apply in general one approximates S by stopping times Sn and restricts Y to cylinder-type functions (see (7.3.1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed form for Y when applying strong markov property
rubrics_metrics.description: Take Y of the form Y_s(ω) = f_0(s) ∏_{m=1}^n f_m(ω(t_m)) where 0 < t1 < ... < tn and f0,...,fn are bounded and continuous (equation (7.3.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This class is used as a core set for which the strong Markov identity is proved; continuity and boundedness permit dominated convergence and induction to show Ex Y_s is a bounded continuous function ϕ(x,s)=E_x Y_s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dominated convergence theorem for kernel continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is bounded and continuous then x → ∫ p_t(x,y) f(y) dy is continuous (so ϕ(x,s)=E_x Y_s is bounded and continuous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dominated convergence justifies interchanging limit and integral; used repeatedly when letting Sn ↓ S and passing limits inside expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation of stopping times by dyadic stopping times
rubrics_metrics.description: Define S_n = ([2^n S] + 1)/2^n as stopping times approximating S from above (Sn ↓ S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows reducing the general strong Markov proof to the discrete-time case and passing to the limit using bounded/ dominated convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone class theorem to extend identity to larger classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H be the collection of Y for which the strong Markov identity holds for all A ∈ F_S; verify H satisfies the monotone class conditions and contains generating sets to conclude H contains desired functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy: verify properties (i),(ii),(iii) for H; approximate indicators of open sets by continuous bounded functions f^n_j ↑ 1_{G_j} to show 1_A ∈ H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping time for hitting Fσ sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an Fσ (countable union of closed sets), then T_A = inf{t : B_t ∈ A} is a stopping time (Exercise 7.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete criterion: hitting times of Fσ sets are measurable w.r.t. the usual filtration and hence stopping times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure properties of stopping times
rubrics_metrics.description: If S and T are stopping times then S ∧ T, S ∨ T, S+T are stopping times; S ∧ t, S ∨ t, S+t are stopping times for deterministic t (Exercise 7.3.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also supremum, infimum, lim sup, lim inf of sequences of stopping times are stopping times (Exercise 7.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of stopping times by patching on events
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a stopping time, A ∈ F_S, and R = S on A and R = ∞ on A^c, then R is a stopping time (Exercise 7.3.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows stoppings can be modified on measurable events while preserving the stopping-time property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurability of comparisons of stopping times
rubrics_metrics.description: For stopping times S and T, the events {S < T}, {S > T}, and {S = T} belong to F_S (and to F_T) (Exercise 7.3.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to localize arguments and to apply conditional expectations on these events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of σ-fields at stopping times
rubrics_metrics.description: For stopping times S and T, F_S ∩ F_T = F_{S ∧ T} (Exercise 7.3.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful identity when combining information at two stopping times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero set properties: no isolated points and measure zero
rubrics_metrics.description: The zero set Z(ω) = {t : B_t(ω) = 0} has no isolated points (almost surely), is uncountable, and has Lebesgue measure zero (Ex(|Z ∩ [0,T]|)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses strong Markov plus Fubini; compares to Cantor set and states Hausdorff dimension is 1/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hitting times Ta have stationary independent increments (under P0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under P_0, {T_a, a ≥ 0} has stationary independent increments: T_b ◦ θ_{T_a} = T_b − T_a and conditioning yields E_0(f(T_b−T_a)|F_{T_a}) = E_0 f(T_{b−a}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: Ta has stable law with index 1/2 (by scaling and classical stable-limit results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling relation for hitting times
rubrics_metrics.description: T_a  ≡_d  a^2 T_1 (equation (7.4.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined with stationary independent increments to deduce limit theorems and Laplace transform forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laplace transform multiplicative property and exponential form
rubrics_metrics.description: ϕ_x(λ) ϕ_y(λ) = ϕ_{x+y}(λ), hence ϕ_a(λ) = exp(−a c(λ)) and homogeneity c(λ) ∝ √λ (leading to formula (7.4.3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify c(λ) by scaling: a c(1) = c(a^2) ⇒ c(λ)=const·√λ; Theorem 7.5.7 gives explicit constant for Brownian motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection principle for Brownian motion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a>0, P_0(T_a < t) = 2 P_0(B_t ≥ a) (equation (7.4.4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorous proof uses strong Markov property with an appropriately chosen functional Y_s(ω) = 1_{s<t, ω(t-s)>a} so that Y_{S}◦θ_S = 1_{T_a < t, B_t > a} and E(Y_S◦θ_S|F_S)=1/2 on {T_a<t}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density formula for hitting time Ta
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from the reflection principle and change of variables; gives explicit density useful in further calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of last zero before 1 (arcsine law)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L = sup{t ≤ 1 : B_t = 0} then P_0(L ≤ s) = (2/π) arcsin(√s) (equation (7.4.7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed by integrating transition densities and changing variables; highlights symmetry and singular behavior at endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional stopping for right-continuous martingales
rubrics_metrics.description: If X_t is a right-continuous martingale adapted to a right-continuous filtration and T is a bounded stopping time, then E X_T = E X_0 (Theorem 7.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses dyadic approximations T_m and discrete-time martingale stopping theorem, then passes to the limit using right continuity and conditional expectation convergence theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brownian motion is a martingale w.r.t. the natural filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: B_t is a martingale with respect to the σ-fields F_t defined earlier (Theorem 7.5.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from the Markov property and symmetry: E_x(B_{t}) = x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional-stopping based exit probability formula
rubrics_metrics.description: If a < x < b then P_x(T_a < T_b) = (b − x)/(b − a) (Theorem 7.5.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: apply optional stopping to B_{T∧t}, let t→∞ and solve linear equation for the exit probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic martingale: B_t^2 − t is a martingale
rubrics_metrics.description: B_t^2 − t is a martingale (Theorem 7.5.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent increments and calculation of conditional second moment to show Ex(B_t^2 | F_s) = B_s^2 + (t − s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected exit time from interval (a,b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T = inf{t : B_t ∉ (a,b)} with a<0<b and starting at 0, then E_0 T = −ab (Theorem 7.5.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine optional stopping on B^2_t − t with exit probabilities to compute expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential martingale criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For any θ, exp(θ B_t − (θ^2 t)/2) is a martingale (Theorem 7.5.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute conditional expectation using independence of increments and normal mgf; used to derive Laplace transforms of hitting times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laplace transform of hitting time (explicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T_a = inf{t : B_t = a} then E_0 exp(−λ T_a) = exp(−a √{2λ}) (Theorem 7.5.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by choosing θ = √{2λ} in the exponential martingale and applying optional stopping with bounded approximations, then letting approximations tend to infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itô's formula (one-dimensional, C^2 condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ C^2 then with probability 1 for all t ≥ 0: f(B_t) − f(B_0) = ∫_0^t f'(B_s) dB_s + (1/2) ∫_0^t f''(B_s) ds (Theorem 7.6.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via Taylor expansion on dyadic partitions, identification of stochastic integral as L^2-limit of Riemann sums, and control of second-order remainder via quadratic variation. Boundedness of derivatives or localization is used to justify limits; extend by truncation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of stochastic integral via L^2 limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For bounded (or suitably square-integrable) adapted integrands g(B_s), define ∫_0^t g(B_s) dB_s as the L^2-limit of approximating Riemann sums I^1_n; the limit is a continuous martingale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key estimates: second-moment computations (E(I_m − I_n)^2) and martingale maximal inequalities; extend from bounded g to general continuous g by localization (stopping at TM = inf{t: |B_t|≥M}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrability condition for stochastic integral to be martingale
rubrics_metrics.description: If g is continuous and E ∫_0^t |g(B_s)|^2 ds < ∞ then M_t = ∫_0^t g(B_s) dB_s is a continuous martingale (Theorem 7.6.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If g fails the integrability condition, the stochastic integral can still be defined as a local martingale via localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itô's formula with time dependence (C^2 in t,x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ C^{1,2} (continuous first t-derivative and second x-derivatives), then f(t,B_t) − f(0,B_0) = ∫_0^t ∂_t f(s,B_s) ds + ∫_0^t ∂_x f(s,B_s) dB_s + (1/2) ∫_0^t ∂_{xx} f(s,B_s) ds (Theorem 7.6.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via polynomial approximation or Taylor expansion on dyadic partitions; control mixed higher-order terms which vanish in the limit because mesh size squared → 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Martingale characterization by the heat equation
rubrics_metrics.description: If u(t,x) satisfies ∂_t u + (1/2) ∂_{xx} u = 0 (e.g., polynomial solutions), then u(t,B_t) is a martingale (Theorem 7.5.8 / Example 7.6.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itô's formula applied to such u cancels the drift term; used to construct polynomial martingales and exponential martingales under parameter choice µ=σ^2/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-dimensional Itô's formula (C^2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ C^2 on R^d then f(B_t) − f(B_0) = ∫_0^t ∂_t f(s,B_s) ds + Σ_{i=1}^d ∫_0^t ∂_{x_i} f(B_s) dB^i_s + (1/2) Σ_{i=1}^d ∫_0^t ∂_{x_i x_i} f(B_s) ds (Theorem 7.6.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross terms for i≠j vanish in the limit because coordinate increments are independent and mean zero; proof begins under bounded second-derivative assumption and removes it by localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skorokhod embedding existence condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If EX = 0 and EX^2 < ∞ then there exists a stopping time T for Brownian motion such that B_T  ≡_d  X and E T = E X^2 (Theorem 8.1.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct embedding by representing distribution F as mixture of two-point (mean-zero) distributions and using hitting times Ta,b for each pair; expectation of the stopping time equals the variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding two-point distributions via exit times
rubrics_metrics.description: If X supported on {a,b} with EX=0 then take T = T_{a,b} = inf{t : B_t ∉ (a,b)}; then B_T  ≡_d  X and E T = −ab (application in Theorem 8.1.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the base case used in the mixture decomposition to embed general distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of iid-embedded sums via independent exit times
rubrics_metrics.description: Given i.i.d. X_i with mean 0 and variance 1, one can construct stopping times T_n with independent increments so that S_n  ≡_d  B(T_n) and the increments T_n − T_{n−1} are i.i.d. (Theorem 8.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent (U,V) mixtures per summand and perform successive exit-time embeddings on a Brownian motion; yields pathwise coupling useful for functional limit theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical CLT from embedding and scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: If X_i i.i.d. mean 0 variance 1 then S_n/√n ⇒ Normal(0,1); proof via embedding: S_n/√n  ≡_d  B(T_n)/√n = W_n(T_n/n) with T_n/n → 1 in probability and W_n(·) ⇒ B(·).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: Brownian scaling, weak law for time-change T_n/n, tightness/continuous mapping to conclude convergence in distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donsker's functional invariance principle conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under i.i.d. mean 0 finite variance assumptions, the rescaled random walk path S(n·)/√n converges weakly to Brownian motion in C[0,1] (Theorem 8.1.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof built from Skorokhod embedding and time-change arguments; continuity of limit functional almost surely and mapping theorem yield convergence of many path functionals (maxima, occupation times, last zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous-mapping principle for path functionals
rubrics_metrics.description: If ψ : C[0,1] → R is continuous P_0-a.s. then ψ(S(n·)/√n) ⇒ ψ(B(·)) (Theorem 8.1.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for examples: maxima (continuous), last zero and occupation times (continuous at almost every Brownian path because set {t: B_t = a} has Lebesgue measure zero a.s.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for continuity points of path functionals
rubrics_metrics.description: A functional ψ(ω) (e.g., last zero sup{t: ω(t)=0}) is continuous at ω if ω has non-isolated zeros around the point of interest and the set {t: ω(t)=a} has zero Lebesgue measure (so many natural functionals are continuous P_0-a.s.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify applying the continuous mapping theorem for occupation times and last-zero functionals; verify exceptional continuity failures have zero probability for Brownian motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-change convergence implies uniform path convergence (lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: If τ^n_{[ns]}/n → s in probability for each s ∈ [0,1] then || S_n,(n·) − B(·) ||_∞ → 0 in probability (Lemma 8.1.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key technical lemma linking convergence of embedded stopping-time clocks to uniform convergence of interpolated paths; used in proving functional CLT via embedding.
